title: UPDATE: Google's Nano Banana 2.1 Takes #4 in Image Benchmarks at Half Cost

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Artificial Analysis ranked Google's Nano Banana 2.1 image model at #4 on both its Text-to-Image and Image-Editing leaderboards, three spots higher than Nano Banana 2. The model is priced at $0.0336 per 1K resolution image, half the cost of its predecessor, and is the lowest-priced model among the top 7 in the T2I v2.0 rankings. On the Arena leaderboard, Nano Banana 2.1 placed #4 in Multi-Image Edit, #5 in Text-to-Image, and #6 in Image Edit, gaining 80 points in text-to-image performance over Nano Banana 2.

Based on Gemini 3.6 Flash, the model takes about 16 seconds per 1K image, compared to 8.3 seconds for Nano Banana 2. It ranks #2 for Productivity & Knowledge Work use cases and improved its standing in human anatomy and layout to #3 and #4 respectively. Nano Banana 2.1 is available through Google AI Studio, Vertex AI, the Gemini app, and third-party providers including Krea, OpenRouter, and fal.

selectedTweets.text:
Google's Nano Banana 2.1 takes #4 on both AA-Image-T2I v2.0 and AA-Image-Editing v2.0, at half the price of Nano Banana 2

Nano Banana 2.1 is Google's new image model, released on October 6. It is based on Gemini 3.6 Flash and replaces Nano Banana 2 (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image) on the Gemini API. It supports both Text to Image and Image Editing in one model. We evaluated Nano Banana 2.1 through the Gemini API at 1K resolution with default settings.

Nano Banana 2.1 is a significant improvement over Nano Banana 2: it ranks higher in all 16 of the generation and editing capabilities we measure, with the largest gains in the Retail & Ecommerce and Productivity & Knowledge Work use cases.

Nano Banana 2.1 is priced at $0.0336 per image ($33.6 per 1k images) at 1K resolution on the Gemini API. That is half the 1K price of Nano Banana 2, and the lowest price among the top 7 models on AA-Image-T2I v2.0. At 2K it costs $0.0504 per image, and at 4K $0.0756 per image.

Nano Banana 2.1 is available in the Gemini app, AI Mode in Search, Google AI Studio, Flow, Stitch, Google Ads and Gemini Enterprise Platform, through the Gemini API and Vertex AI, and on third-party providers.

Congratulations to @GoogleDeepMind & @Google on the release!

See below for our detailed analysis and example outputs of Nano Banana 2.1 in the Artificial Analysis Image Arena 🧵

selectedTweets.bestBit: renamed Nano Banana 2.5 to Nano Banana 2.1 but also changed it from Lite to Flash
selectedTweets.text:
It took them a while because the whole process was a mess.

- June 16: The very first checkpoint, `instant-ramen`, landed on Arena. It was Nano Banana 2 Lite.
- August 28: A new checkpoint called `instant-ramen-v2` was released. It should have been Nano Banana 2.5 Lite.
- August 30: `instant-ramen-v2` was renamed to `spicy-mayo`.
- September 18: Partners got access to `spicy-mayo` via Vertex under the model ID `nano-banana-2.5`.
- October 2: The string `IMAGE_GENERATOR_GEMPIX_2P5_FLASH` appeared in the Google Notebook mobile app.

In the Gemini web and mobile app, the underlying config for Nano Banana 2.1 is called `IMAGE_GENERATOR_GEMPIX_2P5_FLASH`.
This means they not only renamed Nano Banana 2.5 to Nano Banana 2.1 but also changed it from Lite to Flash.

selectedTweets.text:
Nano Banana 2.1 is here, and I’ve prepared a little torture test for Google’s latest image model. 🍌

The update promises better image quality, more accurate text rendering, and better consistency across repeated edits, while keeping the speed and cost efficiency of Nano Banana 2. It supports output up to 4K, multiple reference images, and Google Search grounding.

For the accompanying image, I created a deliberately complex test scene packed with people, objects, readable text, tricky lighting, and reflections. The challenge is getting all those details to make sense together while still looking like a real photograph. Zoom in and inspect the small stuff. How well do you think it handled the challenge?
